newsitem.title: MEXICO: GCC up sharply on U.S. tariff hopes.
newsitem.headline: GCC up sharply on U.S. tariff hopes.

text.p: Shares listed by Mexican cement maker Grupo Cementos de Chihuahua (GCC) had notched up sharp gains in late trade on Friday, on hopes the U.S. Department of Commerce would lower anti-dumping tariffs on imports from Mexico, analysts said.
Traders and analysts said hopes were triggered by a newspaper report the anti-dumping tariff would be cut to 74.42 percent from 103.85 percent.

"It's excellent news," said Jaime Fernandez, an analyst at the Interacciones brokerage. "Apart from that, we need to look at where the stock has been. It recently gained to 9.50 pesos, and then the market hit it hard."
GCC B shares were up 30 centavos in late trade to 7.80 pesos.
GCC is based in northern Mexico and depends heavily on exports to the U.S. market.
